j427.detail: In the smallpox epidemic, the four Fujiwara brothers at the center of government die one after another. The political balance changed.

j428.title: Return to Heijo-kyo
j428.detail: After moving the capital from place to place, to Kuni, Naniwa and Shigaraki, Emperor Shomu returns to Heijo-kyo.

j429.title: Gold Discovered in Mutsu
j429.detail: Gold is found in Mutsu, relieving the shortage of gold for the Great Buddha. The era name also changed to Tenpyo-kampo.

j430.title: Kaifuso
j430.detail: The oldest surviving anthology of Chinese poetry by Japanese. It shows that nobles of the time held Chinese verse as a part of their cultivation.

j431.title: Incident of Tachibana no Naramaro
j431.detail: A plot by Tachibana no Naramaro and others who resisted Fujiwara no Nakamaro's power is discovered, and many are punished.

j432.title: Rebellion of Emi no Oshikatsu
j432.detail: Fujiwara no Nakamaro (Emi no Oshikatsu) clashed with Retired Empress Koken and Dokyo and raised an army, but was defeated and killed.

j433.title: Usa Hachiman Oracle Incident
j433.detail: An oracle arrives saying Dokyo should be put on the throne, but Wake no Kiyomaro verifies it and reports it false.

j434.title: Rebellion of Korehari no Azamaro
j434.detail: Korehari no Azamaro, an Emishi chieftain, kills the inspector of Mutsu. It triggered a prolonged war between the court and the Emishi.

j435.title: Assassination of Fujiwara no Tanetsugu
j435.detail: The official in charge of building Nagaoka-kyo is assassinated, and Crown Prince Sawara is deposed and dies.

j436.title: Shoku Nihongi
j436.detail: Completed as the national history continuing the Nihon Shoki. An important source on the history of the Nara period.

j437.title: Tamuramaro Subdues the Emishi
j437.detail: Sakanoue no Tamuramaro leads a large army on campaign and presses the war against the Emishi of Tohoku.

j438.title: Construction of Isawa Castle
j438.detail: Isawa Castle is built in Iwate as a base for managing Tohoku.

j439.title: Saicho Returns and the Tendai School
j439.detail: Saicho, who studied in Tang, returns and spreads the Tendai school on Mt. Hiei.

j440.title: Kukai Returns and the Shingon School
j440.detail: Kukai, who studied esoteric Buddhism, returns and later opens Kongobu-ji on Mt. Koya.

j441.title: Kusuko Incident
j441.detail: A coup attempted by Retired Emperor Heizei aiming to return to the throne. Emperor Saga put it down, and the Kurodo-dokoro was set up.

j442.title: Kukai Is Given To-ji
j442.detail: Emperor Saga gives To-ji to Kukai as a base for spreading esoteric Buddhism in the capital.

j443.title: Shugei Shuchi-in
j443.detail: A private school Kukai opened in Kyoto. It aimed to be a place where anyone could learn regardless of status.

j444.title: Jowa Incident
j444.detail: The Fujiwara push aside other powerful nobles and replace the crown prince. The dominance of the Northern branch was fixed.

j445.title: Fujiwara no Yoshifusa Becomes Grand Minister
j445.detail: He becomes the first subject to be Grand Minister, laying the foundation for Fujiwara prosperity.

j446.title: Jogan Eruption of Mt. Fuji
j446.detail: Mt. Fuji erupts violently, and flowing lava forms the Aokigahara.

j447.title: Jogan Earthquake
j447.detail: A huge earthquake and tsunami occur off Sanriku. It is compared with the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake.

j448.title: Ako Dispute
j448.detail: Fujiwara no Mototsune protests the wording of Emperor Uda's edict and refuses to conduct government. The position of kampaku is established.

j449.title: Engi Shoen Consolidation Order
j449.detail: A law cracking down on an excess of shoen estates. It was an attempt to rebuild the state's finances.

j450.title: Fall of Tang
j450.detail: Tang falls, and China enters a period of division. Japan reviews its exchange with the continent and turns toward its own culture (Kokufu culture).

j451.title: Engishiki
j451.detail: A code collecting detailed rules for implementing the ritsuryo. A clue to the institutions, rites and products of the time.

j452.title: Kuya's Nembutsu
j452.detail: Kuya, called the Saint of the Marketplace, urged the nembutsu in the streets of Kyoto and spread Pure Land faith among commoners.

j453.title: Kagero Nikki
j453.detail: A diary by the mother of Fujiwara no Michitsuna, recording her feelings and troubles over her husband. A forerunner of diary literature by women.

j454.title: Ojoyoshu
j454.detail: A book in which Genshin explains how to be reborn in the Pure Land. Its depiction of hell greatly influenced people's faith.

j455.title: The Pillow Book
j455.detail: An essay by Sei Shonagon that sharply records court life and her sensitivity to nature.

j456.title: Death of Fujiwara no Michinaga
j456.detail: Michinaga, who composed "This world, I think, is indeed mine; like the full moon, lacking nothing," dies.

j457.title: Taira no Tadatsune's Rebellion
j457.detail: Minamoto no Yorinobu puts down a revolt in Boso. It became a foothold for the Minamoto clan to build power in eastern Japan.

j458.title: First Year of Mappo
j458.detail: It was believed that the world entered the Age of Decline from this year, and anxiety spread. People hoping for rebirth in the Pure Land competed to build temples and Buddhist images.

j459.title: Sarashina Diary
j459.detail: A diary by the daughter of Sugawara no Takasue, covering her life from a girlhood of longing for tales.

j460.title: Accession of Emperor Go-Sanjo
j460.detail: An emperor without Fujiwara maternal relations, who issued a shoen consolidation order among other measures, marking a turning point for regency politics.

j461.title: Enkyu Shoen Consolidation Order
j461.detail: The Records Office was set up to examine shoen documents and weed out improper estates.

j462.title: Konjaku Monogatari-shu
j462.detail: A collection of over a thousand tales from India, China and Japan. It vividly portrays warriors and commoners.

j463.title: Genji Monogatari Emaki
j463.detail: A picture scroll presenting scenes of The Tale of Genji in pictures and text. One of the oldest examples of an emaki.

j464.title: Heike Nokyo
j464.detail: Decorated sutras dedicated to Itsukushima Shrine by Taira no Kiyomori and the Taira family. They convey the aesthetic of the Taira at the height of their glory.

j465.title: Eisai and Chogen Go to Song China
j465.detail: Eisai studied Zen, and Chogen studied architecture and engineering, before returning. They later became a basis of Kamakura Buddhism.

j466.title: Shishigatani Plot
j466.detail: A plan by aides of Retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa to overthrow the Taira is discovered, and those involved are punished.

j467.title: Coup of Jisho 3
j467.detail: Taira no Kiyomori stages a coup, confines Retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa, and establishes Taira rule.

j468.title: Prince Mochihito Raises the Banner
j468.detail: Prince Mochihito, son of Retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa, issues a call to overthrow the Taira. It led to the uprisings of Minamoto no Yoritomo and others.

j469.title: Battle of Ishibashiyama
j469.detail: Minamoto no Yoritomo, having risen, is defeated by Oba Kagechika and others at Ishibashiyama and flees to Awa.

j470.title: Battle of Fujigawa
j470.detail: Minamoto no Yoritomo faces the Taira, and the Taira army is said to have retreated, startled by the sound of waterfowl taking wing.

j471.title: Taira Flee the Capital
j471.detail: Pursued by Kiso Yoshinaka's army, the Taira leave the capital with Emperor Antoku and withdraw to the western provinces.

j472.title: Death of Kiso Yoshinaka
j472.detail: Pursued by Minamoto no Yoritomo's forces, Yoshinaka is killed in battle at Awazu in Omi.

j473.title: Death of Saigyo
j473.detail: The poet Saigyo, a samurai who became a monk, sang of cherry blossoms and travel and left the Sankashu. "May I die in spring beneath the blossoms."

j474.title: Eisai Brings the Rinzai School
j474.detail: Eisai, returned from Song, transmits Zen. He is also known for the Kissa Yojoki, which explained the benefits of tea.

j475.title: Rebuilding Ceremony of Todai-ji
j475.detail: Todai-ji, burned by the Taira, is rebuilt, and Yoritomo attends. Chogen raised funds through solicitation.

j476.title: Jogen Persecution
j476.detail: In the suppression of exclusive nembutsu, Honen is exiled to Tosa and Shinran to Echigo.

j477.title: Wada Rebellion
j477.detail: Wada Yoshimori, chief of the Samurai-dokoro, fights Hojo Yoshitoki and loses, solidifying the Hojo position.

j478.title: Gukansho
j478.detail: A history by Jien that tells history as the shifting of "reason" (dori). Written before the Jokyu War.

j479.title: Shinran's Kyogyoshinsho
j479.detail: A text regarded as the fundamental scripture of Jodo Shinshu. Shinran taught that it is precisely evil people who are saved.

j480.title: Ogura Hyakunin Isshu
j480.detail: A collection of poems by one hundred poets, said to have been chosen by Fujiwara no Teika. Still loved today as karuta cards.

j481.title: The Tale of the Heike
j481.detail: A war tale about the glory and fall of the Taira. Biwa priests recited it and spread it widely.

j482.title: Dogen Opens Eihei-ji
j482.detail: Dogen of the Soto school opens Eihei-ji in Echizen. He taught shikantaza, simply sitting.

j483.title: Hoji Battle
j483.detail: The Hojo destroy the powerful Miura clan, and the Hojo autocratic order is established.

j484.title: Casting of the Kamakura Great Buddha
j484.detail: Casting of the Amida Buddha at Kotoku-in begins. It was originally housed in a Great Buddha Hall, which was lost to tsunamis and other causes.

j485.title: Mongol Letter
j485.detail: A letter demanding submission arrives from Kublai of the Mongol Empire. The shogunate responded with Hojo Tokimune as regent.

j486.title: Marco Polo Sets Out
j486.detail: The Venetian merchant stayed in Yuan China for 17 years. In "The Travels of Marco Polo" he introduced "Zipangu, the land of gold."

j487.title: Ippen Founds the Ji School
j487.detail: He handed out tablets inscribed "Namu Amida Butsu" and traveled the country with dancing nembutsu.

j488.title: Fall of Southern Song
j488.detail: Yuan destroys Southern Song and rules all of China. It then prepared to attack Japan again.

j489.title: Shimotsuki Incident
j489.detail: The powerful vassal Adachi Yasumori is destroyed by the chief steward Taira no Yoritsuna. The despotism of the main Hojo line grew stronger.

j490.title: Heizenmon Rebellion
j490.detail: Regent Hojo Sadatoki destroys Taira no Yoritsuna, the chief steward who had grown tyrannical.

j491.title: Mongol Invasion Scrolls
j491.detail: A picture scroll Takezaki Suenaga, a vassal of Higo, had painted to promote his own military achievements.

j492.title: Essays in Idleness
j492.detail: An essay collection by Priest Kenko, setting down a sense of impermanence and life's wisdom.

j493.title: Emperor Go-Daigo Escapes from Oki
j493.detail: Emperor Go-Daigo, exiled to Oki, escapes, and anti-shogunate momentum surges at once.

j494.title: Nitta Yoshisada Attacks Kamakura
j494.detail: Yoshisada attacks Kamakura from Inamuragasaki, and the Hojo clan takes their own lives at Tosho-ji.

j495.title: Nakasendai Rebellion
j495.detail: Hojo Tokiyuki, son of Hojo Takatoki, retakes Kamakura. Ashikaga Takauji, who marched east to crush it, then turned against the new government.

j496.title: Kemmu Shikimoku
j496.detail: A political program Ashikaga Takauji issued to set out policy for founding a shogunate. It decided to place the shogunate in Kyoto.

j497.title: Jinno Shotoki
j497.detail: A history by Kitabatake Chikafusa arguing the legitimacy of the Southern Court.

j498.title: Taiheiki
j498.detail: A war tale of the turmoil of the Northern and Southern Courts. It later spread in the form of storytelling.

j499.title: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu Becomes Grand Minister
j499.detail: Even after yielding the shogunate to his son, Yoshimitsu became Grand Minister and rose to the highest rank at court as well.

j500.title: Oei Rebellion
j500.detail: Ouchi Yoshihiro rises against Yoshimitsu at Sakai and dies in battle. The suppression of powerful shugo advanced.

j501.title: Yoshimitsu Sends an Envoy to Ming
j501.detail: Yoshimitsu sent an envoy to Ming, received investiture as "King of Japan," and the tally trade later began.

j502.title: Oei Invasion
j502.detail: Korean forces raid Tsushima, regarded as a base of the wako pirates. The So clan later became the contact point with Korea through trade.

j503.title: Founding of the Ryukyu Kingdom
j503.detail: Sho Hashi unifies the Three Kingdoms and builds the Ryukyu Kingdom. It prospered through trade linking China, Japan and Southeast Asia.

j504.title: Eikyo Rebellion
j504.detail: Shogun Ashikaga Yoshinori defeats the Kamakura kubo Ashikaga Mochiuji. Turmoil in Kanto continued.

j505.title: Kyotoku Rebellion
j505.detail: In Kanto, a conflict between the Kamakura kubo and the Kanto kanrei turns into war, and Kanto enters the threshold of the Warring States period.

j506.title: Ota Dokan Builds Edo Castle
j506.detail: Built by Ota Dokan, steward of the Ogigayatsu Uesugi family. Tokugawa Ieyasu later rebuilt it extensively as his base.

j507.title: Sesshu Goes to Ming China
j507.detail: The Zen monk Sesshu crosses to Ming and studies Chinese ink painting. After returning home he perfected a distinctly Japanese ink painting.

j508.title: End of the Onin War
j508.detail: The war that lasted eleven years ends without resolution. Kyoto burned, and the shoen system crumbled.

j509.title: Meio Coup
j509.detail: Hosokawa Masamoto expels Shogun Ashikaga Yoshitane, and the shogun's authority is badly shaken. Taken as the start of the Warring States period.

j510.title: Ryoan-ji Rock Garden
j510.detail: A dry landscape garden with white sand and fifteen stones. A garden that asks of the viewer quiet and imagination.

j511.title: Revival of the Gion Festival
j511.detail: The Gion Festival, interrupted by the Onin War, is revived by the power of the townspeople.

j512.title: Tenbun Hokke Disturbance
j512.detail: The Enryaku-ji on Mt. Hiei burns down the temples of the Hokke (Nichiren) school in Kyoto.

j513.title: Night Battle of Kawagoe
j513.detail: Hojo Ujiyasu defeats the large army of the Kanto kanrei with a small force. Supremacy in Kanto tilts toward the Hojo.

j514.title: Xavier Preaches in Yamaguchi
j514.detail: With Ouchi Yoshitaka's permission he preaches in Yamaguchi, and missionary activity spreads.

j515.title: Fourth Battle of Kawanakajima
j515.detail: Takeda Shingen and Uesugi Kenshin fight their fiercest battle. Both armies suffered many deaths.

j516.title: Nobunaga Enters Gifu Castle
j516.detail: Nobunaga takes the Saito clan's Inabayama Castle, renames it "Gifu," and begins using the seal "Tenka Fubu."

j517.title: Suppression of the Nagashima Ikko-ikki
j517.detail: Oda Nobunaga attacks the Ikko-ikki of Ise Nagashima on a large scale and crushes it.

j518.title: Surrender of Ishiyama Hongan-ji
j518.detail: The eleven-year Ishiyama War ends, and Kennyo leaves Osaka.

j519.title: Kyoto Horse Parade
j519.detail: Nobunaga displays his might by assembling many retainers and horses before the emperor.

j520.title: Fall of the Takeda
j520.detail: The Oda–Tokugawa allied army invades Kai, and Takeda Katsuyori takes his own life at Mt. Temmoku.

j521.title: Battle of Yamazaki
j521.detail: Some ten days after the Honno-ji Incident, Hashiba Hideyoshi defeats Akechi Mitsuhide at Yamazaki.

j522.title: Kiyosu Conference
j522.detail: Oda retainers discuss Nobunaga's successor and the division of his lands after his death. Hideyoshi took the lead.

j523.title: Battle of Komaki and Nagakute
j523.detail: Hashiba Hideyoshi fights Oda Nobukatsu and Tokugawa Ieyasu. Ieyasu won the local fighting, but Hideyoshi outplayed him in politics.

j524.title: Hideyoshi Becomes Kampaku
j524.detail: Hideyoshi is appointed kampaku, and the next year receives the surname Toyotomi and becomes Grand Minister.

j525.title: Imperial Visit to Jurakudai
j525.detail: Emperor Go-Yozei visits Hideyoshi's Jurakudai, and the daimyo swear loyalty to Hideyoshi.

j526.title: Odawara Campaign
j526.detail: Hideyoshi attacks the Hojo, completing the unification of the country.

j527.title: Ieyasu Enters Edo
j527.detail: Tokugawa Ieyasu, moved to Kanto by Hideyoshi's order, makes Edo his base.

j528.title: Keicho-Fushimi Earthquake
j528.detail: A great earthquake strikes Kyoto and Fushimi, and the keep of Fushimi Castle collapses. Hideyoshi escaped harm.

j529.title: San Felipe Incident
j529.detail: Remarks by the crew of a ship that drifted ashore in Tosa angered Hideyoshi and led to the execution of missionaries.

j530.title: Cherry-Blossom Viewing at Daigo
j530.detail: A grand blossom-viewing party Hideyoshi held late in life, just a few months before his death.

j531.title: Itowappu System
j531.detail: The shogunate created a system in which designated merchants bought up in bulk the raw silk brought in by Portuguese traders.

j532.title: Ieyasu Passes the Shogunate to Hidetada
j532.detail: After only two years, he yielded the shogunate to his son, showing that the Tokugawa would hold the office by heredity.

j533.title: Joseon Missions to Japan
j533.detail: From Joseon Korea in the Edo period, an embassy visited Japan at each change of shogun.

j534.title: Edict Banning Christianity
j534.detail: The shogunate bans Christianity in its own territories, and extends this nationwide the next year.

j535.title: Keicho Embassy to Europe
j535.detail: Date Masamune of Sendai sends Hasekura Tsunenaga. He visited Europe and met the Pope in Rome.

j536.title: Death of Tokugawa Ieyasu
j536.detail: He dies at Sunpu and is later enshrined at Nikko Toshogu.

j537.title: Tokugawa Iemitsu Becomes Shogun
j537.detail: He styled himself a "born shogun." He solidified the foundations of the shogunate-domain system, including alternate attendance and the closed-country policy.

j538.title: Purple Robe Incident
j538.detail: The shogunate intervenes in the court's appointment of monks, and the emperor abdicates. The shogunate's superiority is settled.

j539.title: Nikko Toshogu Completed
j539.detail: The present magnificent shrine buildings are completed. Edo culture also put effort into expressing authority.

j540.title: Ban on Permanent Sale of Farmland
j540.detail: To prevent farmers from losing their land and falling into ruin, the sale of fields was banned.

j541.title: Keian Edict
j541.detail: Said to set out rules of conduct for farmers' lives, but doubt remains whether the shogunate issued it.

j542.title: Tamagawa Aqueduct Completed
j542.detail: A waterworks drawing water from the Tama River to Edo is completed. It supported the giant city of Edo.

j543.title: Shakushain's War
j543.detail: An Ainu chief rises up against the unfair trading of the Matsumae domain but is defeated.

j544.title: The Japanese Family Storehouse
j544.detail: Ihara Saikaku's representative townsman tale, depicting the lives of merchants.

j545.title: Death of Matsuo Basho
j545.detail: He dies in Osaka while on a journey. "Fallen ill on a journey, my dreams roam over withered fields."

j546.title: Shotoku Reforms
j546.detail: Arai Hakuseki advances political reforms based on Confucianism under Tokugawa Ienobu and Ietsugu.

j547.title: Kaihaku Goshi Shinrei
j547.detail: Limited the number of ships and the value of trade in Nagasaki trade. A system to prevent the outflow of gold and silver.

j548.title: Death of Ogata Korin
j548.detail: Known for works such as "Red and White Plum Blossoms" screens. A painter of the Rinpa school.

j549.title: Koishikawa Infirmary
j549.detail: Prompted by a letter to the suggestion box, a facility is set up to treat poor sick people free of charge.

j550.title: Dojima Rice Exchange Recognized
j550.detail: Futures trading in rice is officially recognized at Dojima in Osaka. Regarded as one of the world's earliest futures markets.

j551.title: Kansei Ban on Heterodoxy
j551.detail: Neo-Confucianism is made the orthodox learning, and teaching other schools in shogunate schools is banned.

j552.title: Toshusai Sharaku Appears
j552.detail: A painter who in only some ten months drew distinctive portraits of actors and then disappeared.

j553.title: Hizakurige
j553.detail: Jippensha Ikku humorously describes the journey of Yaji and Kita. It lit the spark of a travel boom.

j554.title: Rezanov Arrives
j554.detail: The Russian envoy Rezanov comes to Nagasaki and requests trade, but the shogunate refuses.

j555.title: Mamiya Rinzo Explores Sakhalin
j555.detail: Rinzo confirms that Sakhalin is an island and explores the Mamiya Strait.

j556.title: Golovnin Incident
j556.detail: Golovnin, a Russian naval captain, is detained on Kunashir Island. After this incident, tension with Russia continued.

j557.title: Nanso Satomi Hakkenden
j557.detail: A long novel Kyokutei Bakin wrote over 28 years. A representative Edo yomihon.

j558.title: Siebold Comes to Japan
j558.detail: The German physician Siebold comes to Dejima in Nagasaki and teaches Dutch learning at the Narutaki school.

j559.title: Siebold Incident
j559.detail: His attempt to take a map of Japan out of the country is discovered, and he is expelled.

j560.title: Opium War
j560.detail: Qing's defeat by Britain shocked Japan too, and the shogunate reviewed its foreign policy.

j561.title: Nagasaki Naval Training Center
j561.detail: Shogunate retainers learn Western naval technology from Dutch instructors.

j562.title: One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
j562.detail: A late series by Utagawa Hiroshige. Its bold compositions influenced Western painters such as Van Gogh.

j563.title: Teradaya Incident
j563.detail: Radicals of the Satsuma domain are cut down by fellow domain samurai acting on Shimazu Hisamitsu's orders.

j564.title: Bunkyu Embassy to Europe
j564.detail: Fukuzawa Yukichi and others accompanied the mission the shogunate sent to Europe and broadened their knowledge of the West.

j565.title: Coup of August 18
j565.detail: The Aizu and Satsuma domains drive the Choshu domain, of the sonno joi (revere the emperor, expel the barbarians) faction, from Kyoto.

j566.title: Choshu's Kozan-ji Uprising
j566.detail: Takasugi Shinsaku rises at Kozan-ji, seizes control of the domain and moves toward overthrowing the shogunate.

j567.title: Second Choshu Expedition
j567.detail: The shogunate army attacks Choshu but is beaten by the modernized Choshu army, and the shogunate's prestige collapses.

j568.title: Ee ja nai ka
j568.detail: People danced through the streets chanting "ee ja nai ka." It spread to many regions amid social unrest.

j569.title: Battle of Toba-Fushimi
j569.detail: Fighting between former shogunate forces and the new government army begins and develops into the Boshin War.

j570.title: Charter Oath
j570.detail: "Deliberative assemblies shall be widely established, and all matters decided by public discussion." The new government's basic policy is set out.

j571.title: Separation of Shinto and Buddhism Order
j571.detail: A policy separating Shinto and Buddhism. It led to haibutsu kishaku, the destruction of temples and Buddhist statues in many places.

j572.title: Capital Moved to Tokyo
j572.detail: The emperor moves to Tokyo, and Edo Castle becomes the Imperial Palace. Ezo was also renamed "Hokkaido."

j573.title: Commoners Permitted Surnames
j573.detail: Commoners, who until then could not publicly use a family name, were allowed to take surnames, which later became compulsory.

j574.title: Postal System Begins
j574.detail: On Maejima Hisoka's proposal, a modern postal service begins in Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka.

j575.title: Edict Allowing Haircuts and Removal of Swords
j575.detail: Cutting off the topknot was permitted. "Tap a cropped head and you hear the sound of civilization and enlightenment."

j576.title: Tomioka Silk Mill
j576.detail: A state-run silk-reeling factory introducing French technology. It was later inscribed as a World Heritage Site.

j577.title: Adoption of the Solar Calendar
j577.detail: The lunar calendar was replaced by the solar calendar, and the 3rd day of the 12th month of Meiji 5 became the 1st day of the 1st month of Meiji 6.

j578.title: Removal of the Anti-Christian Notice Boards
j578.detail: After protests from Europe and America, the notice boards banning Christianity were taken down and it was tacitly tolerated.

j579.title: Taiwan Expedition
j579.detail: The government sends troops to Taiwan, citing the killing of shipwrecked Ryukyuans.

j580.title: Ganghwa Island Incident
j580.detail: A Japanese warship is fired on at Ganghwa Island in Korea and returns fire. It led to the Japan–Korea Treaty of Amity the following year.

j581.title: Japan–Korea Treaty of Amity
j581.detail: An unequal treaty that made Korea open ports and granted Japan extraterritoriality.

j582.title: Sapporo Agricultural College
j582.detail: Clark is said to have left the words "Boys, be ambitious." It trained people for developing Hokkaido.

j583.title: Haitorei (Sword Ban)
j583.detail: Wearing swords was forbidden to all but soldiers and police officers. The samurai class lost its privileges one by one.

j584.title: Ryukyu Disposition
j584.detail: The Ryukyu Domain is abolished and Okinawa Prefecture is established. The Ryukyu Kingdom came to its end.

j585.title: Political Crisis of 1881
j585.detail: In a dispute over opening a national assembly, Okuma Shigenobu is expelled from the government. Ito Hirobumi and others take the lead.

j586.title: Bank of Japan Opens
j586.detail: Established as the central bank amid Matsukata Masayoshi's fiscal consolidation.

j587.title: Chichibu Incident
j587.detail: Farmers impoverished by the Matsukata deflation rise up in Chichibu. One of the most violent events of the Freedom and People's Rights Movement.

j588.title: Normanton Incident
j588.detail: An incident in which Japanese passengers were said to have been abandoned when a British ship sank. Criticism of extraterritoriality grew.

j589.title: Ukigumo
j589.detail: Futabatei Shimei's novel, written in a style close to spoken language, a pioneer of the modern novel.

j590.title: Mori Ogai's "The Dancing Girl"
j590.detail: A novel based on his experience studying in Germany. It portrays the struggles of the modern self.

j591.title: Otsu Incident
j591.detail: The Russian crown prince, visiting Japan, is attacked. An incident that tested the independence of the judiciary.

j592.title: Higuchi Ichiyo's "Takekurabe"
j592.detail: It depicts boys and girls growing up beside the licensed quarter. A work from just before her death at age 24.

j593.title: Public Order and Police Law
j593.detail: A law that sharply cracked down on labor movements and political activity.

j594.title: Botchan
j594.detail: Natsume Soseki's novel, drawing on his experience as a teacher in Matsuyama.

j595.title: South Manchuria Railway Company
j595.detail: A railway company Japan ran after the Russo-Japanese War. It became a foothold for advancing into Manchuria.

j596.title: Magazine Seito Launched
j596.detail: Known for the opening of Hiratsuka Raicho's founding statement: "In the beginning, woman was truly the sun."

j597.title: High Treason Incident
j597.detail: Kotoku Shusui and 11 others are executed for plotting to assassinate the emperor. Suppression of the socialist movement grew stronger.

j598.title: Japan's First Olympic Participation
j598.detail: At the Stockholm Games, Kanakuri Shiso in the marathon and Mishima Yahiko in the sprint compete.

j599.title: Taisho Political Crisis
j599.detail: A popular movement under the slogan "Destroy the clique, protect constitutional government" topples the Katsura Taro cabinet.

j600.title: Yoshino Sakuzo's Minponshugi
j600.detail: The idea of reflecting the people's will in politics even under imperial sovereignty. It gave Taisho Democracy its theoretical support.

j601.title: Hara Takashi's Full Party Cabinet
j601.detail: Hara Takashi, the "commoner prime minister" with no peerage, forms the first full-fledged party cabinet.

j602.title: Paris Peace Conference
j602.detail: At the peace conference after World War I, Japan took part as one of the five great powers. Its racial equality proposal was not adopted.

j603.title: First National Census
j603.detail: A population survey conducted nationwide at the same time. It has been carried out every five years since.

j604.title: First May Day
j604.detail: About 10,000 workers gather in Ueno Park, Tokyo.

j605.title: Assassination of Hara Takashi
j605.detail: Hara is stabbed to death at Tokyo Station. Distrust of party politics spread.

j606.title: Three-Party Kenseikai Cabinet
j606.detail: As a result of the Second Movement to Protect the Constitution, a party cabinet is formed with Kato Takaaki as prime minister.

j607.title: Peace Preservation Law
j607.detail: It punished associations aiming to alter the national polity or deny the system of private property. Its scope was later expanded.

j608.title: Dawn of Showa
j608.detail: On December 25, the death of Emperor Taisho brings the change to Showa. The first year of Showa lasted only seven days.

j609.title: London Naval Treaty
j609.detail: A treaty limiting holdings of auxiliary ships. Criticism of an infringement of the supreme command arose.

j610.title: Showa Depression
j610.detail: Under the effects of the Great Depression and lifting the gold embargo, a severe slump set in, and farm villages suffered especially.

j611.title: Emperor Organ Theory Incident
j611.detail: Minobe Tatsukichi's theory is attacked and his books banned. Freedom of speech narrowed.

j612.title: National Mobilization Law
j612.detail: A law letting the government control people and supplies for war.

j613.title: Nomonhan Incident
j613.detail: Japan and the Soviet Union clash on the Manchuria–Mongolia border, and the Japanese army suffers heavy losses.

j614.title: Imperial Rule Assistance Association
j614.detail: Political parties are dissolved and unified into one organization for mobilizing the people for war.

j615.title: Student Mobilization
j615.detail: The draft deferment for humanities students is ended, and a send-off rally is held at Jingu Gaien.

j616.title: School Children's Evacuation
j616.detail: To avoid air raids, city children are evacuated in groups to rural areas.

j617.title: Acceptance of the Potsdam Declaration
j617.detail: The Allies' call to surrender is accepted, and the decision to end the war is made.

j618.title: Occupation and Dissolution of the Zaibatsu
j618.detail: Under Allied occupation, Japan's democratization and demilitarization were pursued. Breaking up the zaibatsu was one part of it.

j619.title: Land Reform
j619.detail: Land is bought from landlords and sold to tenant farmers, creating many owner-farmers.

j620.title: Women Vote for the First Time
j620.detail: In the first postwar general election, women exercised the right to vote for the first time, and 39 women were elected to the Diet.

j621.title: Fundamental Law of Education
j621.detail: Set the basics of education in line with the ideals of the new constitution. The 6-3-3-4 school system also began around this time.

j622.title: Yukawa Hideki's Nobel Prize
j622.detail: Japan's first Nobel Prize. A theoretical physicist who predicted the existence of the meson.

j623.title: Dodge Line
j623.detail: The American adviser Dodge called for austerity to curb inflation.

j624.title: Golden Lion for Rashomon
j624.detail: Kurosawa Akira's film wins the top prize at the Venice Film Festival, and Japanese cinema became known to the world.

j625.title: The Film Godzilla
j625.detail: A monster film set against the backdrop of H-bomb tests. It became a landmark of special-effects cinema.

j626.title: "The Postwar Is Over"
j626.detail: A phrase from the Economic White Paper became a buzzword, symbolizing the completion of postwar recovery and the start of high growth.

j627.title: Income Doubling Plan
j627.detail: The Ikeda cabinet announces a plan to double national income in ten years.

j628.title: Japan–Korea Basic Treaty
j628.detail: Japan and South Korea normalize diplomatic relations.

j629.title: The Beatles Visit Japan
j629.detail: They performed at the Nippon Budokan and greatly influenced youth culture.

j630.title: Basic Law for Environmental Pollution Control
j630.detail: The basic law addressing pollution such as Minamata disease, Itai-itai disease and Yokkaichi asthma.

j631.title: Second-Largest GNP in the World
j631.detail: Japan's gross national product becomes second only to the US among capitalist countries.

j632.title: University Disputes
j632.detail: At the University of Tokyo and elsewhere, the Zenkyoto carried out a student movement.

j633.title: Normalization of Japan–China Relations
j633.detail: Prime Minister Tanaka Kakuei visits China and signs a joint communique.

j634.title: Sapporo Winter Olympics
j634.detail: Asia's first Winter Olympics. Japan's ski jumpers, called the "Hinomaru squadron," swept gold, silver and bronze.

j635.title: Lockheed Scandal
j635.detail: Former Prime Minister Tanaka Kakuei is arrested on suspicion of bribery over aircraft sales.

j637.title: Tsukuba Science Expo
j637.detail: Held on the theme "Man, Dwelling and Environment, Science and Technology," it drew over 20 million visitors.

j638.title: Equal Employment Opportunity Law
j638.detail: A law to eliminate discrimination between men and women in recruitment, hiring and promotion.

j639.title: Seikan Tunnel and Seto Ohashi Bridge
j639.detail: Honshu is connected to Hokkaido and to Shikoku by rail.

j640.title: Consumption Tax Introduced
j640.detail: It began at a rate of 3%.

j641.title: Gulf War and Minesweeper Dispatch
j641.detail: After the Gulf War, Self-Defense Forces minesweepers were sent to the Persian Gulf. The first overseas mission.

j642.title: PKO Cooperation Law
j642.detail: The Self-Defense Forces became able to take part in UN peacekeeping operations.

j643.title: J.League Kicks Off
j643.detail: Opening with ten clubs, soccer's popularity spread all at once.

j644.title: Nagano Winter Olympics
j644.detail: The second Winter Olympics held in Japan.

j645.title: Kyushu-Okinawa Summit
j645.detail: A G8 summit held in Nago, Okinawa.

j646.title: Aichi Expo
j646.detail: "Love the Earth Expo." Held on an environmental theme.

j647.title: Postal Privatization
j647.detail: The Koizumi cabinet's postal privatization law passes. The LDP won a landslide in the House of Representatives dissolution and general election.

j648.title: Hayabusa Returns
j648.detail: After seven years, it completes its journey of bringing back sand from the asteroid Itokawa.

j649.title: Mt. Fuji Becomes a World Heritage Site
j649.detail: It was inscribed as a World Cultural Heritage Site as an "object of faith and wellspring of art."

j650.title: Voting Age Lowered to 18
j650.detail: The voting age was lowered from 20 to 18.

j651.title: Consumption Tax Raised to 10%
j651.detail: A reduced tax rate was introduced.

j652.title: State of Emergency
j652.detail: Declared for the first time amid the spread of COVID-19, with requests to stay home.

j653.title: Shooting of Former PM Abe
j653.detail: Former Prime Minister Abe Shinzo is shot and killed while giving a speech in Nara.

j654.title: COVID-19 Reclassified to Category 5
j654.detail: Its status under the Infectious Diseases Act changed to "Category 5," and behavioral restrictions ended.

j655.title: Japan Wins the WBC
j655.detail: Japan's national team wins the World Baseball Classic for the third time.

j656.title: New Banknotes Issued
j656.detail: New bills bearing portraits of Shibusawa Eiichi, Tsuda Umeko and Kitasato Shibasaburo are issued.

izanagi.name: Izanagi
izanagi.detail: Together with Izanami he bore the Japanese archipelago; returning from the land of the dead he purified himself and bore Amaterasu and others.
izanagi.lesson: Drawing a line, and starting afresh.
izanagi.label: Age of the Gods

izanami.name: Izanami
izanami.detail: She bore the land and the gods with Izanagi, but died giving birth to the fire god and became ruler of the land of the dead.
izanami.label: Age of the Gods

amaterasu.name: Amaterasu
amaterasu.detail: Goddess who rules the High Plain of Heaven. She hid in the rock cave and darkened the world, then reappeared through the gods' wisdom. Ancestral deity of the imperial house.
amaterasu.lesson: Light can be called back by everyone's effort.
amaterasu.label: Age of the Gods

susanoo.name: Susanoo
susanoo.detail: Expelled from the High Plain of Heaven for his violence, he slew the Yamata no Orochi, became a hero, and built a palace in Izumo.
susanoo.lesson: Even the unruly have a role.
susanoo.label: Age of the Gods

okuninushi.name: Okuninushi
okuninushi.detail: He advanced the building of Izumo, later yielded the land and was enshrined at Izumo Taisha. Also known as a god of matchmaking.
okuninushi.lesson: Yielding is also a leader's decision.
okuninushi.label: Age of the Gods

ninigi.name: Ninigi
ninigi.detail: Grandson of Amaterasu. He received the Three Sacred Treasures and descended to Takachiho.
ninigi.label: Age of the Gods

tsukuyomi.name: Tsukuyomi
tsukuyomi.detail: The moon god born from Izanagi's purification. He rules the world of night.
tsukuyomi.label: Age of the Gods

yamasachi.name: Yamasachihiko (Hoori)
yamasachi.detail: He lost his brother's fishhook, went to the sea god's palace, gained jewels that control the tides, and subdued his brother.
yamasachi.label: Age of the Gods

jimmu.name: Emperor Jimmu
jimmu.detail: The first emperor according to the Nihon Shoki and Kojiki. Said to have marched east from Hyuga to Yamato and taken the throne at Kashihara Palace. The date follows the Nihon Shoki tradition.
jimmu.lesson: Read tradition as a story that tells the shape of a country.

himiko.name: Himiko
himiko.detail: She united the country through shamanic rites, sent envoys to Wei and received the title "King of Wa, Friend of Wei."
himiko.lesson: She tried to settle conflict through authority and diplomacy.

shotoku.name: Prince Shotoku
shotoku.detail: He established the Twelve-Level Cap and Rank System and the Seventeen-Article Constitution, and sent missions to Sui China.
shotoku.lesson: He tried to put the state in order through law and rank.

suiko.name: Empress Suiko
suiko.detail: An empress of the Asuka period. She governed with her nephew Prince Shotoku as regent.

soga.name: Soga no Umako
soga.detail: He gained power by marrying into the imperial family and advanced the acceptance of Buddhism.

naka.name: Prince Naka no Oe
naka.detail: He led the Taika Reforms and later took the throne as Emperor Tenji.

kamatari.name: Nakatomi no Kamatari
kamatari.detail: He teamed up with Prince Naka no Oe to bring down the Soga and was granted the surname Fujiwara.

tenmu.name: Emperor Tenmu
tenmu.detail: He won the Jinshin War, took the throne, and built the framework of the ritsuryo state.

gyoki.name: Gyoki
gyoki.detail: He preached to the common people and led the building of bridges and ponds. He later helped with the Great Buddha.

shomu.name: Emperor Shomu
shomu.detail: Amid continuing plague and rebellion, he vowed the provincial temples and the Great Buddha of Todai-ji.

ganjin.name: Ganjin
ganjin.detail: Though blind, he reached Japan on his sixth attempt and transmitted the monastic precepts.

abe.name: Abe no Nakamaro
abe.detail: He crossed to Tang, became an official, and ended his life there without being able to return.

saicho.name: Saicho
saicho.detail: Studied in Tang and founded the Tendai school on Mt. Hiei.

kukai.name: Kukai
kukai.detail: Studied esoteric Buddhism in Tang and opened Mt. Koya. He was also skilled in calligraphy and engineering.

sugawara.name: Sugawara no Michizane
sugawara.detail: Demoted to Dazaifu, he was later enshrined as a god of learning.

michinaga.name: Fujiwara no Michinaga
michinaga.detail: He made his daughters empresses one after another and built the height of regency government.
michinaga.lesson: Concentrating power can also sow the seeds of later backlash.

shikibu.name: Murasaki Shikibu
shikibu.role: Author of The Tale of Genji
shikibu.detail: While serving at court, she wrote one of the world's oldest long novels.

shonagon.name: Sei Shonagon
shonagon.detail: With a sharp eye, she set down the days of the court in essays.

goshirakawa.name: Retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa
goshirakawa.detail: He ran cloistered government and maneuvered skillfully through the Genpei turmoil.

kiyomori.name: Taira no Kiyomori
kiyomori.detail: First warrior to become Chancellor, he promoted Japan–Song trade.
kiyomori.lesson: He linked the rise of the warriors with overseas trade, but monopoly drew resentment.

yoritomo.name: Minamoto no Yoritomo
yoritomo.detail: He opened warrior government in Kamakura and built the system of shugo and jito.

yoshitsune.name: Minamoto no Yoshitsune
yoshitsune.detail: Active in the campaign against the Taira, he fell out with his brother Yoritomo and took his own life in Oshu.

masako.name: Hojo Masako
masako.detail: Yoritomo's wife. In the Jokyu War she rallied the vassals and saved the shogunate in crisis.

shinran.name: Shinran
shinran.detail: He taught that anyone is saved through the nembutsu and won wide support among the common people.

dogen.name: Dogen
dogen.detail: He studied in Song and taught shikantaza, simply sitting.

nichiren.name: Nichiren
nichiren.detail: Valuing the Lotus Sutra, he criticized other schools and made appeals to the shogunate.

tokimune.name: Hojo Tokimune
tokimune.detail: He rejected the Yuan demand for submission and prepared for the two invasions of Bun'ei and Koan.

godaigo.name: Emperor Go-Daigo
godaigo.detail: He overthrew the Kamakura shogunate and ruled directly, but it collapsed in a short time.

kusunoki.name: Kusunoki Masashige
kusunoki.detail: Serving Emperor Go-Daigo, he ran rings around shogunate forces at Chihaya Castle and elsewhere.

takauji.name: Ashikaga Takauji
takauji.detail: He clashed with Emperor Go-Daigo, founded the shogunate, and brought on the turmoil of the Northern and Southern Courts.

yoshimitsu.name: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu
yoshimitsu.detail: He united the Northern and Southern Courts, began trade with Ming, and built the Golden Pavilion.

zeami.name: Zeami
zeami.detail: With his father Kan'ami he brought Noh to maturity and wrote the Fushikaden.

ikkyu.name: Ikkyu Sojun
ikkyu.detail: An unconventional Zen monk. He satirized authority and was loved by the common people.

sesshu.name: Sesshu
sesshu.detail: He went to Ming, studied ink painting, and perfected Japanese landscape painting.

yoshimasa.name: Ashikaga Yoshimasa
yoshimasa.detail: He brought on the Onin War, yet nurtured the Higashiyama culture typified by the Silver Pavilion.

soun.name: Hojo Soun
soun.detail: He won Izu and Odawara and is seen as a leading example of gekokujo (the low overthrowing the high).

nobunaga.name: Oda Nobunaga
nobunaga.detail: He made use of firearms and set the economy moving with rakuichi-rakuza. He fell at Honno-ji.
nobunaga.lesson: Those who use new technology and the economy move an age. But if you earn too much resentment, you lose the ground beneath you.

hideyoshi.name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
hideyoshi.detail: Rising from a peasant to kampaku, he fixed social status through land surveys and the sword hunt.

ieyasu.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
ieyasu.detail: He won at Sekigahara and built the framework for a peace lasting 260 years.
ieyasu.lesson: Patience and building institutions produced long stability.

rikyu.name: Sen no Rikyu
rikyu.detail: He brought wabi tea to maturity, but Hideyoshi ordered him to commit seppuku.

shingen.name: Takeda Shingen
shingen.detail: A Sengoku daimyo of Kai. He fought Uesugi Kenshin at Kawanakajima.

kenshin.name: Uesugi Kenshin
kenshin.detail: The Dragon of Echigo. He valued righteousness and fought Shingen at Kawanakajima.

masamune.name: Date Masamune
masamune.detail: The one-eyed lord of Tohoku. He sent Hasekura Tsunenaga to explore trade with Europe.

mitsuhide.name: Akechi Mitsuhide
mitsuhide.detail: He killed Nobunaga at Honno-ji but was defeated at the Battle of Yamazaki.

mitsunari.name: Ishida Mitsunari
mitsunari.detail: He led the Western Army at Sekigahara and lost.

iemitsu.name: Tokugawa Iemitsu
iemitsu.detail: He set up alternate attendance and the closed-country system, solidifying shogunate rule.

basho.name: Matsuo Basho
basho.detail: He raised haikai to an art and left famous verses on his journey of "Narrow Road to the Deep North."

chikamatsu.name: Chikamatsu Monzaemon
chikamatsu.detail: A playwright for puppet theater and kabuki. He wrote of the tragic love of townspeople.

yoshimune.name: Tokugawa Yoshimune
yoshimune.detail: He restored finances in the Kyoho Reforms and encouraged practical learning and the suggestion box.

gennai.name: Hiraga Gennai
gennai.detail: Also a naturalist, a versatile man who reconstructed the elekiter.

genpaku.name: Sugita Genpaku
genpaku.detail: He translated the Kaitai Shinsho and laid the foundation of Dutch learning.

tadataka.name: Ino Tadataka
tadataka.detail: Starting to study at fifty, he walked the whole country and made an accurate map of Japan.

hokusai.name: Katsushika Hokusai
hokusai.detail: Known for works such as Thirty-six Views of Mt. Fuji. He sought to master his art until the age of ninety.
hokusai.lesson: An attitude of learning even as the years pass.

ii.name: Ii Naosuke
ii.detail: He pushed the opening of the country but was assassinated outside the Sakurada Gate after the Ansei Purge.

shoin.name: Yoshida Shoin
shoin.detail: At the Shoka Sonjuku he trained Takasugi Shinsaku and others, and was executed in the Ansei Purge.
shoin.lesson: Education produced the generation that carried out change.

kaishu.name: Katsu Kaishu
kaishu.detail: He sailed to America on the Kanrin Maru and agreed with Saigo on the bloodless surrender of Edo Castle.

ryoma.name: Sakamoto Ryoma
ryoma.detail: Through mediating the Satsuma–Choshu Alliance and his Eight-Point Plan on shipboard, he envisioned the shape of a new country.

saigo.name: Saigo Takamori
saigo.detail: He achieved the surrender of Edo but was later defeated in the Satsuma Rebellion.

yoshinobu.name: Tokugawa Yoshinobu
yoshinobu.detail: He carried out the Restoration of Imperial Rule and later lived for his hobbies.

meiji.name: Emperor Meiji
meiji.detail: From the Charter Oath to the promulgation of the constitution, he became a symbol of building the modern state.

fukuzawa.name: Fukuzawa Yukichi
fukuzawa.detail: He wrote An Encouragement of Learning and founded Keio Gijuku.
fukuzawa.lesson: "Independence and self-respect": knowledge is the foundation of the self-reliance of individuals and the nation.

ito.name: Ito Hirobumi
ito.detail: He led the drafting of the Constitution of the Empire of Japan and became the first prime minister.

itagaki.name: Itagaki Taisuke
itagaki.role: Leader of the Freedom and People's Rights Movement
itagaki.detail: Remembered for "Itagaki may die, but liberty will never die."

shibusawa.name: Shibusawa Eiichi
shibusawa.detail: He took part in founding hundreds of companies, such as the First National Bank, and is called the "father of Japanese capitalism."
shibusawa.lesson: Morality and economy go together: "The Analects and the Abacus."

tsuda.name: Tsuda Umeko
tsuda.detail: A girl student who went to America at six. She founded the predecessor of Tsuda University.

higuchi.name: Higuchi Ichiyo
higuchi.detail: She wrote works such as Takekurabe and died at twenty-four.

soseki.name: Natsume Soseki
soseki.detail: In I Am a Cat and Kokoro, he portrayed the loneliness of modern people.

akiko.name: Yosano Akiko
akiko.detail: Poet of "Midaregami." During the Russo-Japanese War she published "Kimi shinitamau koto nakare" ("You must not die").

noguchi.name: Noguchi Hideyo
noguchi.detail: He worked on research into yellow fever and died after being infected in Africa.

hara.name: Hara Takashi
hara.detail: The "commoner prime minister" who formed the first full-fledged party cabinet. He was assassinated at Tokyo Station.

showa.name: Emperor Showa
showa.detail: He reigned for a turbulent sixty-four years and became a symbol after the war.

yoshida.name: Yoshida Shigeru
yoshida.detail: A postwar prime minister. He signed the San Francisco Peace Treaty and the US–Japan Security Treaty.

konosuke.name: Matsushita Konosuke
konosuke.detail: Founder of Panasonic. Called the "god of management" for his "water supply philosophy."

soichiro.name: Honda Soichiro
soichiro.detail: He founded Honda and challenged the world with technology.

yukawa.name: Yukawa Hideki
yukawa.detail: The first Japanese to win a Nobel Prize (Physics).

tezuka.name: Tezuka Osamu
tezuka.detail: Known for works like Astro Boy. He laid the foundations of Japanese anime and manga.

kurosawa.name: Kurosawa Akira
kurosawa.detail: Known for works like Seven Samurai. He influenced world cinema.

hibari.name: Misora Hibari
hibari.detail: A singer representing the Showa era. "Like a Flowing River" was her signature song in later years.

tanaka.name: Tanaka Kakuei
tanaka.detail: He achieved the normalization of relations with China and advocated "Remodeling the Japanese Archipelago."

nukata.name: Princess Nukata
nukata.detail: A leading poet of the early Man'yoshu, known for poems linked to the two emperors Tenji and Tenmu. Her dates of birth and death are unknown.

jito.name: Empress Jito
jito.detail: Empress consort of Emperor Tenmu. Carrying out her husband's wishes she put the Asukakiyomihara Code into force and built Fujiwara-kyo.

genmei.name: Empress Genmei
genmei.detail: The empress of the era that saw the move to Heijo-kyo, the completion of the Kojiki and the issue of Wado Kaichin.

hitomaro.name: Kakinomoto no Hitomaro
hitomaro.detail: A leading court poet of the Man'yoshu. He left powerful expression in his long poems (choka). Also called the Saint of Poetry.

okura.name: Yamanoue no Okura
okura.detail: He composed poems for the poor and for children. Known for the "Dialogue on Poverty."

tabito.name: Otomo no Tabito
tabito.detail: As governor of Dazaifu, he formed the Tsukushi poetry circle with Yamanoue no Okura and others. He is said to have held the "Plum Blossom Banquet."

yakamochi.name: Otomo no Yakamochi
yakamochi.detail: Said to be one of the compilers of the Man'yoshu, which contains the most poems by him.

komyo.name: Empress Komyo
komyo.detail: Empress consort of Emperor Shomu. She is said to have set up the Hiden'in and Segyakuin to help the poor and the sick.

fuhito.name: Fujiwara no Fuhito
fuhito.detail: He took part in compiling the Taiho and Yoro codes and laid the foundation of Fujiwara prosperity.

nagaya.name: Prince Nagaya
nagaya.detail: Minister of the Left in the early Nara period. He clashed with the Fujiwara and took his own life under suspicion of treason.

kibi.name: Kibi no Makibi
kibi.detail: He studied in Tang as a member of the missions and after returning served Shomu, Koken and Shotoku.

kammu.name: Emperor Kanmu
kammu.detail: He moved the capital to Nagaoka-kyo and then Heian-kyo and sought strong imperial authority, including military campaigns against the Emishi.

tamuramaro.name: Sakanoue no Tamuramaro
tamuramaro.detail: The first Seii Taishogun. He brought the Emishi leader Aterui and others to surrender.

saga.name: Emperor Saga
saga.detail: Counted with Kukai and Tachibana no Hayanari among the "Three Brushes." He loved culture and Chinese poetry.

ennin.name: Ennin
ennin.detail: A disciple of Saicho. He went to Tang and wrote the travel diary "Record of a Pilgrimage to Tang in Search of the Law."

enchin.name: Enchin
enchin.detail: A monk of the Tendai school. He studied esoteric Buddhism in Tang and later revived Onjo-ji (Mii-dera).

narihira.name: Ariwara no Narihira
narihira.detail: Thought to be the model for the hero of the Tales of Ise. One of the Six Poetic Immortals.

tsurayuki.name: Ki no Tsurayuki
tsurayuki.detail: One of the compilers of the Kokin Wakashu. With the Tosa Diary he opened the way for diary literature in kana.

masakado.name: Taira no Masakado
masakado.detail: He rose in Kanto and styled himself "New Emperor," but was killed by Fujiwara no Hidesato and others.

kuya.name: Kuya
kuya.detail: "The Saint of the Marketplace," who walked the streets spreading the nembutsu.

genshin.name: Genshin
genshin.detail: In the Ojoyoshu he depicted the Pure Land and hell, and sparked Pure Land faith.

yorimichi.name: Fujiwara no Yorimichi
yorimichi.detail: Succeeding his father Michinaga, he served as regent and kampaku for 50 years and built Byodo-in at Uji.

shirakawa.name: Retired Emperor Shirakawa
shirakawa.detail: He began cloistered rule. He is said to have remarked that the Kamo River's waters, the dice of sugoroku, and warrior monks were beyond his control.

yoshiie.name: Minamoto no Yoshiie
yoshiie.detail: Active in the Former Nine Years' and Later Three Years' Wars. Called "Hachiman Taro," he became a symbol of the later heads of the Minamoto.

kiyohira.name: Fujiwara no Kiyohira
kiyohira.detail: After the Later Three Years' War he built Chuson-ji at Hiraizumi and sought peace in Oshu.

saigyo.name: Saigyo
saigyo.detail: Formerly a guard of the Northern Palace. He took vows and composed poems while traveling the provinces. The Sankashu.

yoshinaka.name: Kiso Yoshinaka
yoshinaka.detail: He rose in Shinano and drove the Taira from the capital. Soon after he was defeated by Yoshitsune and others.

shigemori.name: Taira no Shigemori
shigemori.detail: Kiyomori's eldest son. He agonized while trying to mediate between his father and Retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa.

unkei.name: Unkei
unkei.detail: He made the Kongo Rikishi at the Great South Gate of Todai-ji with Kaikei and others. A representative of realist Kamakura sculpture.

eisai.name: Eisai
eisai.detail: He brought the Rinzai school from Song, along with tea seeds and the custom of drinking tea.

honen.name: Honen
honen.detail: He taught that one is saved by reciting "Namu Amida Butsu" and founded the Jodo school.

chomei.name: Kamo no Chomei
chomei.detail: Born into a family of Shimogamo Shrine priests, he later took vows and wrote the Hojoki.

teika.name: Fujiwara no Teika
teika.detail: Compiler of the Shin Kokin Wakashu. Said to have assembled the Ogura Hyakunin Isshu.

yoshitoki.name: Hojo Yoshitoki
yoshitoki.detail: He defeated Retired Emperor Go-Toba in the Jokyu War and solidified the Hojo regency.

sanetomo.name: Minamoto no Sanetomo
sanetomo.detail: Gifted at waka poetry, he left the Kinkai Wakashu. He was assassinated at Tsurugaoka Hachiman-gu.

yasutoki.name: Hojo Yasutoki
yasutoki.detail: He enacted the Goseibai Shikimoku and set standards of law for the warriors.

ippen.name: Ippen
ippen.detail: He traveled the country spreading the nembutsu, known for the dancing nembutsu.

kenko.name: Priest Kenko
kenko.detail: Author of Essays in Idleness. He first served the court and later took vows.

yoshisada.name: Nitta Yoshisada
yoshisada.detail: He attacked Kamakura and destroyed the Hojo. He later clashed with Ashikaga Takauji and was defeated.

tadayoshi.name: Ashikaga Tadayoshi
tadayoshi.detail: He built the shogunate with his elder brother Takauji, but later fell out and set off the Kanno Disturbance.

chikafusa.name: Kitabatake Chikafusa
chikafusa.detail: He supported the Southern Court. In the Jinno Shotoki he argued its legitimacy.

yoshinori.name: Ashikaga Yoshinori
yoshinori.detail: He aimed at autocratic rule but was assassinated in the Kakitsu Incident.

rennyo.name: Rennyo
rennyo.detail: He revived Jodo Shinshu (Hongan-ji) and spread the teaching through plain letters (ofumi).

katsumoto.name: Hosokawa Katsumoto
katsumoto.detail: He became commander-in-chief of the Eastern Army in the Onin War.

sozen.name: Yamana Sozen
sozen.detail: Commander-in-chief of the Western Army in the Onin War. Also called the "Red Monk."

tomiko.name: Hino Tomiko
tomiko.detail: Wife of Ashikaga Yoshimasa. It is said that her attempt to make her son shogun was one cause of the Onin War.

yoshimoto.name: Imagawa Yoshimoto
yoshimoto.detail: He governed Suruga, Totomi and Mikawa. He was killed by Oda Nobunaga at Okehazama.

motonari.name: Mori Motonari
motonari.detail: He won at Itsukushima and ruled the Chugoku region. Also known for the tale of the "three arrows."

dosan.name: Saito Dosan
dosan.detail: The "Viper of Mino," said to have risen from oil seller to lord of Mino. His daughter Nohime was Nobunaga's wife.

motochika.name: Chosokabe Motochika
motochika.detail: He came close to unifying Shikoku from Tosa but surrendered to Hideyoshi.

yoshihisa.name: Shimazu Yoshihisa
yoshihisa.detail: Head of the Shimazu clan. He conquered most of Kyushu but surrendered to Hideyoshi.

ujiyasu.name: Hojo Ujiyasu
ujiyasu.detail: Third head of the Odawara Hojo. He won the Night Battle of Kawagoe and extended his power in Kanto.

yoshikage.name: Asakura Yoshikage
yoshikage.detail: A daimyo of Echizen. He clashed with Nobunaga and was destroyed.

nagamasa.name: Azai Nagamasa
nagamasa.detail: He married Nobunaga's younger sister Oichi but later fought Nobunaga and lost.

katsuie.name: Shibata Katsuie
katsuie.detail: A senior retainer who served Nobunaga. He was defeated by Hideyoshi at the Battle of Shizugatake.

toshiie.name: Maeda Toshiie
toshiie.detail: He served Nobunaga and Hideyoshi and laid the foundation of the million-koku Kaga domain.

kanbe.name: Kuroda Kanbe
kanbe.detail: As Hideyoshi's strategist he supported the Chugoku campaign and the unification of the country.

hanbei.name: Takenaka Hanbei
hanbei.detail: A strategist who served Hideyoshi. He died of illness at a young age.

yukimura.name: Sanada Nobushige (Yukimura)
yukimura.detail: In the Siege of Osaka he fought hard, nearly reaching Tokugawa Ieyasu's headquarters. He was praised as "the best warrior in Japan."

tadakatsu.name: Honda Tadakatsu
tadakatsu.detail: One of the Four Guardians of the Tokugawa. He is said to have fought in 57 battles without suffering even a scratch.

kiyomasa.name: Kato Kiyomasa
kiyomasa.detail: One of the Seven Spears of Shizugatake. He later built Kumamoto Castle.

xavier.name: Francis Xavier
xavier.detail: He landed at Kagoshima in 1549 and first brought Christianity to Japan.

musashi.name: Miyamoto Musashi
musashi.detail: A two-sword master. In his later years he wrote The Book of Five Rings. Also known as a painter.

eitoku.name: Kano Eitoku
eitoku.detail: He painted the wall and screen paintings of Azuchi and Osaka castles. A representative of the lavish Momoyama style.

koetsu.name: Hon'ami Koetsu
koetsu.detail: Skilled in calligraphy, ceramics and maki-e lacquer, he opened an artists' village at Takagamine in Kyoto.

hidetada.name: Tokugawa Hidetada
hidetada.detail: Succeeding Ieyasu, he solidified the foundations of the shogunate, including issuing the Laws for the Military Houses.

shiro.name: Amakusa Shiro
shiro.detail: A boy regarded as the commander of the Shimabara Rebellion.

masayuki.name: Hoshina Masayuki
masayuki.detail: Half-brother of Tokugawa Iemitsu. He supported the young fourth shogun Ietsuna and improved things such as the Tamagawa Aqueduct.

mitsukuni.name: Tokugawa Mitsukuni
mitsukuni.detail: "Mito Komon." He began the compilation of the Dai Nihonshi.

tsunayoshi.name: Tokugawa Tsunayoshi
tsunayoshi.detail: He encouraged learning, and is also known for the Laws of Compassion for Living Things.

saikaku.name: Ihara Saikaku
saikaku.detail: A writer of ukiyo-zoshi describing the lives of Osaka townspeople.

hakuseki.name: Arai Hakuseki
hakuseki.detail: He served the sixth and seventh shoguns and carried out the Shotoku Reforms. He wrote the Seiyo Kibun.

tadasuke.name: Ooka Tadasuke
tadasuke.detail: Trusted by Yoshimune, as Edo's city magistrate he organized things such as the town fire brigades. "Ooka Echizen."

okitsugu.name: Tanuma Okitsugu
okitsugu.detail: He pursued policies that valued commerce. Opinions of him are divided after his fall.

sadanobu.name: Matsudaira Sadanobu
sadanobu.detail: He carried out the Kansei Reforms.

norinaga.name: Motoori Norinaga
norinaga.detail: He wrote the Kojiki-den and discussed "mono no aware," the ancient heart of Japan.

buson.name: Yosa Buson
buson.detail: A haiku poet who made painterly verses, and also a painter of the Nanga school.

issa.name: Kobayashi Issa
issa.detail: Known for down-to-earth verses such as "Thin frog, don't give up—Issa is here."

hiroshige.name: Utagawa Hiroshige
hiroshige.detail: He won popularity with landscapes such as the Fifty-three Stations of the Tokaido.

bakin.name: Kyokutei Bakin
bakin.detail: He completed the Nanso Satomi Hakkenden over 28 years. Blind in later life, he kept writing by dictation.

koan.name: Ogata Koan
koan.detail: He opened the Tekijuku in Osaka and trained people such as Fukuzawa Yukichi and Omura Masujiro.

choei.name: Takano Choei
choei.detail: He criticized the shogunate's policy of repelling foreign ships and was imprisoned in the Bansha no Goku.

oshio.name: Oshio Heihachiro
oshio.detail: He rose up in an attempt to save the people during the famine.

sontoku.name: Ninomiya Sontoku
sontoku.detail: Born to a farm family in Odawara, he devoted himself to reviving farm villages. Known for the image of a boy reading while carrying firewood.

rinzo.name: Mamiya Rinzo
rinzo.detail: He confirmed that Sakhalin is an island. The origin of the name "Mamiya Strait."

mizuno.name: Mizuno Tadakuni
mizuno.detail: He carried out the Tenpo Reforms.

abe_m.name: Abe Masahiro
abe_m.detail: As chief senior councillor when Perry arrived, he practiced a politics of hearing broad opinion.

kido.name: Kido Takayoshi (Katsura Kogoro)
kido.detail: A leader of Choshu. He formed the Satsuma–Choshu Alliance and after the Restoration advanced the return of the domain registers and abolition of domains. One of the "Three Great Nobles of the Restoration."

takasugi.name: Takasugi Shinsaku
takasugi.detail: He created the Kiheitai and led Choshu toward overthrowing the shogunate. He died of illness at 27.

okubo.name: Okubo Toshimichi
okubo.detail: From Satsuma. A central figure after the Restoration, he promoted industrial development. One of the "Three Great Nobles of the Restoration."

iwakura.name: Iwakura Tomomi
iwakura.detail: He served as ambassador of the Iwakura Mission.

kondo.name: Kondo Isami
kondo.detail: Commander of the Shinsengumi, who kept order in Kyoto.

hijikata.name: Hijikata Toshizo
hijikata.detail: Vice-commander of the Shinsengumi. In the Boshin War he fought to the end and died in battle at Hakodate.

okita.name: Okita Soji
okita.detail: Regarded as a master swordsman. He died young of tuberculosis.

nariakira.name: Shimazu Nariakira
nariakira.detail: He started modern industry through the Shuseikan projects and discovered talents such as Saigo Takamori.

nakaoka.name: Nakaoka Shintaro
nakaoka.detail: He worked with Sakamoto Ryoma for the Satsuma–Choshu Alliance. He was attacked together with Ryoma at the Omiya in Kyoto.

okuma.name: Okuma Shigenobu
okuma.detail: He founded Tokyo Senmon Gakko (later Waseda University). He served as prime minister.

yamagata.name: Yamagata Aritomo
yamagata.detail: He worked on building the conscription system and is called the "father of the national army."

mutsu.name: Mutsu Munemitsu
mutsu.detail: As foreign minister he achieved the abolition of extraterritoriality, part of the unequal treaties (1894).

komura.name: Komura Jutaro
komura.detail: He handled the peace of the Russo-Japanese War (Treaty of Portsmouth) and the restoration of tariff autonomy.

togo.name: Togo Heihachiro
togo.detail: He defeated the Baltic Fleet in the Battle of Tsushima.

nogi.name: Nogi Maresuke
nogi.detail: He commanded the siege of Port Arthur. He followed Emperor Meiji in death.

ogai.name: Mori Ogai
ogai.detail: While serving as Surgeon General of the Army, he wrote works such as "The Dancing Girl" and "Takasebune."

shiki.name: Masaoka Shiki
shiki.detail: He pushed the reform of haiku and tanka. He kept writing "Byosho Rokushaku" on his sickbed.

takuboku.name: Ishikawa Takuboku
takuboku.detail: He composed "A Handful of Sand" amid a life of poverty. He died of illness at 26.

akutagawa.name: Akutagawa Ryunosuke
akutagawa.detail: He wrote short stories such as "Rashomon," "The Nose," and "The Spider's Thread."

kitasato.name: Kitasato Shibasaburo
kitasato.detail: He succeeded in pure culture of the tetanus bacillus and also discovered the plague bacillus.

uchimura.name: Uchimura Kanzo
uchimura.detail: He advocated the Non-Church Movement and wrote works such as "Representative Men of Japan."

nitobe.name: Nitobe Inazo
nitobe.detail: He wrote "Bushido" in English and also served as Under-Secretary-General of the League of Nations.

tenshin.name: Okakura Tenshin
tenshin.detail: He took part in founding the Tokyo School of Fine Arts and introduced Japanese beauty to the world through "The Book of Tea" in English.

tanaka_s.name: Tanaka Shozo
tanaka_s.detail: He raised the Ashio copper mine pollution case in the Imperial Diet and in a direct appeal to the emperor.

raicho.name: Hiratsuka Raicho
raicho.detail: In the magazine Seito she declared, "In the beginning, woman was truly the sun."

kenji.name: Miyazawa Kenji
kenji.detail: Known for "Night on the Galactic Railroad" and "Ame ni mo makezu." He devoted himself to the farmers of Iwate.

yamamoto.name: Yamamoto Isoroku
yamamoto.detail: As commander-in-chief of the Combined Fleet he directed the Pearl Harbor attack. He was killed in action while inspecting the southern front.

tojo.name: Tojo Hideki
tojo.detail: Prime minister at the outbreak of the Pacific War. After the war he was sentenced to death at the Tokyo Trial.

shidehara.name: Shidehara Kijuro
shidehara.detail: He promoted cooperative diplomacy. After the war, as prime minister, he took part in drafting the new constitution.

korekiyo.name: Takahashi Korekiyo
korekiyo.detail: As finance minister he sought a way out of the Showa Depression but was assassinated in the February 26 Incident.

inukai.name: Inukai Tsuyoshi
inukai.detail: Leaving the words "If we talk, you'll understand," he was assassinated in the May 15 Incident.

kato_t.name: Kato Takaaki
kato_t.detail: He passed the Universal Manhood Suffrage Law.

kawabata.name: Kawabata Yasunari
kawabata.detail: Known for "The Izu Dancer" and "Snow Country." The first Japanese Nobel laureate in Literature.

mishima.name: Mishima Yukio
mishima.detail: Known for "The Temple of the Golden Pavilion" and "The Sound of Waves." In 1970 he committed seppuku at the Self-Defense Forces Ichigaya base.

dazai.name: Dazai Osamu
dazai.detail: Known for "No Longer Human" and "Run, Melos!"

ozu.name: Ozu Yasujiro
ozu.detail: "Tokyo Story." Known for his low-angle shots from a low camera position.

rikidozan.name: Rikidozan
rikidozan.detail: In postwar Japan, he became the hero of the pro-wrestling boom.

taro.name: Okamoto Taro
taro.detail: "Art is explosion!" He created the Tower of the Sun for Expo '70 in Osaka.

tange.name: Tange Kenzo
tange.detail: He designed the Yoyogi National Gymnasium and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building.

ikeda.name: Ikeda Hayato
ikeda.detail: He advanced rapid economic growth under the "Income Doubling Plan."

sato.name: Sato Eisaku
sato.detail: He achieved the return of Okinawa and announced the Three Non-Nuclear Principles. He received the Nobel Peace Prize.

nakasone.name: Nakasone Yasuhiro
nakasone.detail: He pushed the breakup and privatization of the National Railways.

tomonaga.name: Tomonaga Shin'ichiro
tomonaga.detail: He received the Nobel Prize in Physics for the theory of renormalization.

nagashima.name: Nagashima Shigeo
nagashima.detail: "Mr. Pro Baseball." He starred as a central batter for the Giants.

miyazaki.name: Miyazaki Hayao
miyazaki.detail: Known for "My Neighbor Totoro" and "Spirited Away."

yamanaka.name: Yamanaka Shinya
yamanaka.detail: He created iPS cells and received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

ohtani.name: Ohtani Shohei
ohtani.detail: With his "two-way" play as pitcher and batter, he is starring in Major League Baseball.
